title: Meet Russia
description: Travel to Russia with Spark and Mango: a country in Eastern Europe whose capital is Moscow, where people speak Russian and pay with the Russian ruble — plus two places we'd love to visit.

body.heading: Where in the world is Russia?
paragraphs: Russia is a country in Eastern Europe, which is part of Europe.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Russia is Moscow.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: The language you will hear most in Russia is Russian.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Russia is the Russian ruble.

body.heading: How big is Russia?
paragraphs: Russia covers about 17,124,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. It is the largest country in the whole world — so wide that it stretches across eleven time zones.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: Red Square holds Russia's most famous view: St Basil's swirling candy-coloured domes, the Kremlin walls and Lenin's mausoleum, beside the GUM arcades.
Saint Petersburg is a city of palaces and canals — the Hermitage museum alone could fill weeks, and its white nights glow in midsummer.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Find Russia on a map or globe. Which continent is it on — and can you name a country that sits next to it?
2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?

takeaway: Russia in one breath: a country in Eastern Europe, capital Moscow, where people speak Russian and pay with the Russian ruble.
materials: A globe, atlas or world map (to find Russia)
Paper and crayons or pencils for the screen-free mission
supervision: Confident readers can read alone; a grown-up can join in for the Think and talk questions about Russia.
safetyNotes: Reading only — no physical activity is involved.
The two visit ideas are daydreams for a future family trip to Russia — real trips always need grown-up planning.
screenFreeExtension: Screen-free mission: find Russia on a map or globe, say its capital out loud, then draw the place you'd most love to visit there.
